claim: StepCoder's Fine-Grained Optimization masks unexecuted (test-uncovered) code tokens out of the PPO loss so only test-verified code spans receive policy-gradient credit, establishing test-coverage-granular reward shaping for code RL as of early 2024.
stance_target: novelty of using per-test/per-requirement execution granularity to shape RL reward signal for code generation
scope_conditions: PPO-based RL from compiler feedback for code generation, APPS+ dataset, Feb 2024
quoted_support: FGO masks unexecuted tokens in unit tests and only computes the loss function using executed tokens to provide fine-grained optimization.

claim: Since unit tests may not cover complicated generated code, optimizing LLMs using unexecuted code snippets is ineffective, motivating StepCoder's curriculum and coverage-masking approach.
stance_target: motivation for execution-coverage-aware RL reward design in code generation
scope_conditions: RL from compiler/test feedback for code generation, long/complex programs
quoted_support: The lengthy code generated by LLMs in response to complex human requirements makes RL exploration a challenge, and since unit tests may not cover the complicated code, optimizing LLMs by using unexecuted code snippets is ineffective.
